title: Staggered fintech adoption on loan default rates

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
I will use a Difference-in-Differences (DiD) approach. The treatment is fintech adoption by period 4, creating a simple before/after comparison between treated and control banks. The key assumption is parallel trends - that treated and control banks would have followed similar trajectories in default rates absent the fintech adoption. I'll test this with pre-treatment trend analysis and include robustness checks.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(lfe)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s08_data.csv")

# Basic data inspection
print("Data summary:")
print(summary(data))

# Create time periods relative to treatment (period 4)
data$time_to_treat <- data$period - 4

# Main DiD specification with unit and time fixed effects
did_model <- felm(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period | 0 | unit_id, data = data)

print("Main DiD Results:")
print(summary(did_model))

# Extract and print the key coefficient
did_coef <- did_model$coefficients["treat_x_post"]
did_se <- did_model$cse["treat_x_post"]
print(paste("DiD Coefficient:", round(did_coef, 4)))
print(paste("Standard Error:", round(did_se, 4)))
print(paste("T-statistic:", round(did_coef/did_se, 2)))

# Test for pre-treatment parallel trends
# Create event study specification
data$treat_period_1 <- ifelse(data$treated == 1 & data$period == 1, 1, 0)
data$treat_period_2 <- ifelse(data$treated == 1 & data$period == 2, 1, 0)
data$treat_period_3 <- ifelse(data$treated == 1 & data$period == 3, 1, 0)
data$treat_period_5 <- ifelse(data$treated == 1 & data$period == 5, 1, 0)
data$treat_period_6 <- ifelse(data$treated == 1 & data$period == 6, 1, 0)
data$treat_period_7 <- ifelse(data$treated == 1 & data$period == 7, 1, 0)
data$treat_period_8 <- ifelse(data$treated == 1 & data$period == 8, 1, 0)

# Event study regression (period 4 is omitted as reference)
event_study <- felm(y ~ treat_period_1 + treat_period_2 + treat_period_3 + 
                    treat_period_5 + treat_period_6 + treat_period_7 + treat_period_8 | 
                    unit_id + period | 0 | unit_id, data = data)

print("Event Study Results (testing parallel trends):")
print(summary(event_study))

# Test joint significance of pre-treatment coefficients
pre_treat_coefs <- c("treat_period_1", "treat_period_2", "treat_period_3")
if(all(pre_treat_coefs %in% names(event_study$coefficients))) {
  print("Pre-treatment coefficients:")
  for(coef in pre_treat_coefs) {
    print(paste(coef, ":", round(event_study$coefficients[coef], 4)))
  }
}

# Robustness check: Simple two-period DiD (pre vs post)
data_robust <- data %>%
  mutate(post_treatment = ifelse(period >= 5, 1, 0)) %>%
  mutate(treat_x_post_robust = treated * post_treatment)

robust_did <- felm(y ~ treat_x_post_robust | unit_id + period | 0 | unit_id, data = data_robust)

print("Robustness Check - Alternative Post-Treatment Definition:")
print(summary(robust_did))

robust_coef <- robust_did$coefficients["treat_x_post_robust"]
print(paste("Robust DiD Coefficient:", round(robust_coef, 4)))

# Calculate descriptive statistics by treatment status
desc_stats <- data %>%
  group_by(treated, post) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_default = mean(y, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_obs = n(),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

print("Descriptive Statistics by Treatment and Post:")
print(desc_stats)

# Calculate simple difference-in-differences manually for verification
treated_post <- desc_stats$mean_default[desc_stats$treated == 1 & desc_stats$post == 1]
treated_pre <- desc_stats$mean_default[desc_stats$treated == 1 & desc_stats$post == 0]
control_post <- desc_stats$mean_default[desc_stats$treated == 0 & desc_stats$post == 1]
control_pre <- desc_stats$mean_default[desc_stats$treated == 0 & desc_stats$post == 0]

manual_did <- (treated_post - treated_pre) - (control_post - control_pre)
print(paste("Manual DiD calculation:", round(manual_did, 4)))

print(paste("Final Result: Fintech adoption effect on default rates:", round(did_coef, 4)))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a negative coefficient of approximately -0.05 to -0.15, indicating that fintech adoption reduced loan default rates by 5-15 percentage points. This makes economic sense because algorithmic credit scoring should improve risk assessment accuracy, leading to better loan origination decisions and lower default rates. The magnitude reflects that while fintech can meaningfully improve lending outcomes, default rates are influenced by many factors beyond just scoring technology, so the effect would be economically significant but not dramatically large.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Staggered DID (Callaway-Sant'Anna or Sun-Abraham) — cohort-specific ATTs; treatment=fintech adoption
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Fintech-adopting banks reduce default rates relative to non-adopters
